1#_: That it is not forbidden from the Torah is permitted for benefit. Maharshal chapter 25 siman 100 disagrees with this and with what Rambam and Mordechai wrote; he holds it is reasonable to be stringent for benefit. And we have only the words of Rishonim and Acharonim.
3#א: Permitted in cooking and benefit. Tur wrote: but pure meat in impure milk or the reverse, and wild animal meat, etc. — is only rabbinically forbidden and permitted in cooking, etc. Beit Yosef challenged: if one species is impure it is forbidden in eating d'oraisa — why decree basar b'chalav eating prohibition? Derishah and Orach Chaim resolve there is practical difference regarding piece becoming nevelah — R' Ephraim siman 92 holds only with meat and milk; and another difference. Acharonim wondered why Sages decreed since already forbidden for impure meat — where hinted? Possibly tanna teaches pure domestic meat in impure milk permitted in cooking and benefit — that 'permitted in cooking and benefit' is superfluous; should say merely permitted — clear it refers to eating; when eating impure thing we need precision that eating forbidden because of basar b'chalav. In any case clear from Mishnah: impure domestic animal permitted cooking and benefit; Rashi did not mention eating permitted since impurity prohibition exists — learn without impurity no basar b'chalav connection; if not tanna would mention; rather plain impure species like other prohibitions; clear Tur's 'only rabbinically' refers only to fowl, not impure meat/milk together — only regarding permitted in benefit and cooking as Beit Yosef; Mechaber well did not copy this; Orach Chaim wrote incorrect; it appears to me law is clear; per Maharshal's correction in Tur before 'and wild animal' — Tur intends only to teach leniency in cooking and benefit.
3#ב: But fish, etc. Beit Yosef wrote nevertheless do not eat fish in milk because of danger — error; should be with meat as Orach Chaim siman 173; Darkei Moshe confused Beit Yosef here; Levush copied Beit Yosef incorrectly.
3#ג: As explained above siman 66 regarding blood. Darkei Moshe and sage general rule 62: Maharshal learned from fish blood to forbid fowl in almond milk without almonds for marit ayin; rejected — no proof from blood which has karet unlike rabbinic fowl in milk; even domestic animal forbidden only by cooking — no marit ayin concern; Rama's words correct and custom spread; nevertheless l'chatchila place almonds by fowl too; where no almonds do not forbid eating — all we can fix we fix; no worse than woman's milk where marit ayin concerned; where no almonds do not forbid eating like woman's milk nearby; Rama's wording implies b'dieved or impossible to place does not block eating.
4#_: And it appears per this, etc. Darkei Moshe left Rashba's words on woman's milk in wonder — not a fortiori from impure milk permitted in cooking; his view here is very astonishing; in Torat HaBayit Rashba explicitly permitted impure milk in cooking and benefit without marit ayin; it appears they did not decree marit ayin except where each alone is permitted to eat — then resembles pure meat and milk; therefore with almond milk l'chatchila place almonds; woman's milk permitted when separated as siman 81 — forbidden to cook with meat for marit ayin; unlike impure milk or meat — no resemblance to pure basar b'chalav — no decree there; clear per my opinion; though I cannot lenient regarding what Rama stringent; nevertheless plain one must forbid marit ayin cooking fowl in milk — Sages decreed explicitly; for one tanna truly d'oraisa; Darkei Moshe: fowl in milk worse than impure in milk — not as Levush who permits marit ayin because recognizable — sometimes cut unrecognizable; viewer cannot distinguish fowl from domestic meat; actually dispute of tannaim; Maharshal chapter 25 siman 52: more concern lest say fowl in milk permitted like R' Yosi HaGelili; Rama's l'chatchila here and nearby regarding dead milk for cooking — be careful where no great need; for medical need without danger may permit cooking in milk where eating prohibition only rabbinic — all the more impure milk or meat.
5#_: And permitted to eat it in milk. Maharshal challenged: why unlike Rashba/Tur siman 86 striking chicken on tail — if entangled in sinews like meat from living; answered: different there d'oraisa eiver min ha'chai prohibition; here Mechaber wrote not completed — even with yolk and white fit for milk even entangled; reason: no meat taste at all; when struck while entangled considered meat from living — not taste-dependent; Maharshal: strained for law — whenever entangled considered meat for all matters; Mahari Weil: women practice prohibition even hard shell; l'chatchila stringent; b'dieved when shell complete even white membrane suffices — no meat law; see siman 87 regarding salting these eggs in name of Maharshal.
9#_: And some forbid. Meaning clear only; Rabbenu Tam and Rashi forbid even dried — not mere excrement; Rama ruled like Rabbenu Tam; Maharshal chapter 25 siman 107 like Rashi: great leniency to permit dried — who knows measure of drying; possibly only if dried with no moisture at all; primary like Rashi.
10#א: That it was salted in stomach. Measure to stand in salting to count as boiling — siman 69 seif 18; salting measure as boiling — siman 91 seif 5.
10#ב: Forbidden to set rennet in it. Meaning do not use that salted/stood-one-day milk to curdle other milk for cheese.
10#ג: Until sixty in milk. Difficult per Rosh siman 108: min b'mino in sixty as Beit Yosef; here salting context — Rosh holds salting forbids only peel measure; cooking needs sixty; say since milk here like oil prohibition forbids whole piece per siman 105; though end siman 105 Rashba etc. — Rosh and Tur disagree; siman 105 seif 7 implies milk not like oil prohibition — investigate; resolve: pickled forbidden entirely per Rosh; salting in vessel measure siman 69; Beit Yosef here proves; Tur/Beit Yosef only full day; Rav hagahah follows his view all salting in sixty as siman 105.
10#ד: And if stomach was dried it does not forbid. Mere excrement; nevertheless forbids meat taste absorbed in excrement — Beit Yosef: second taste permitting first like fish in bowl; Darkei Moshe disagrees — not second taste; absorbed taste in milk is first taste.
11#א: One who set rennet in skin, etc. Meaning placed piece of skin in milk.
11#ב: This-and-this causes. Learned from Mordechai: Rabbenu baruch permitted — presumably did not set all pot milk from forbidden stomach only from dried; not customary to put stomach in pot; sometimes more dried — this-and-this causes; permitted; if prohibition cannot leaven alone without permitted — all permit; if prohibition alone can leaven — not this-and-this causes; Mordechai: if prohibition alone cannot leaven without help — permitted; Abaye Avodah Zarah 49 — this-and-this causes only if neither alone can leaven; if prohibition alone can — help does not help; Tosafot there explicitly; here clear dried cannot set alone — cannot rely on this-and-this causes without proof no clear in stomach; Mordechai's words require study.
